richPins.summary: Product metadata is in place, so Rich Pins (product type) will work. The domain is not claimed yet, so that is the one blocking owner step.

checked.og:title: present
checked.og:image: present (2000x2000 on the fluted velvet page)
checked.schemaProductOffer: present (JSON-LD Product with Offer, availability InStock)
checked.robotsTxt: User-agent * Allow / (Pinterest's crawler is not blocked)

missing: Domain not claimed on Pinterest: no p:domain_verify meta tag on the home page and no Pinterest tag found.
No Pinterest business account confirmed as linked to the store (GA4 shows only 12 Pinterest sessions in 3 months).
Optional og:availability / product:availability meta tag is absent (JSON-LD already gives InStock, so this is not blocking).
ownerSteps: 1. Check first whether a Pinterest account already exists: GA4 shows a 'Pinterest / organic' source, which suggests someone has already shared tagged links. Reuse that account if you have it.

2. Business account: go to pinterest.co.uk/business/create and sign up with the Eagle Bed email (or, in an existing personal account, Settings > Account management > Convert to a business account). Business name 'Eagle Bed', website www.eaglebed.co.uk, country United Kingdom, category Home decor / Retail.
3. In Shopify admin: Settings > Apps and sales channels > Shopify App Store, search 'Pinterest' (the app by Pinterest), Add sales channel, then Connect and log in to the Pinterest business account.

4. In the Pinterest app inside Shopify, follow the setup steps: it claims www.eaglebed.co.uk for you, installs the Pinterest tag and starts the product catalog sync. If asked, turn on the Pinterest app embed in Online Store > Themes > Customise > App embeds (this is a live theme change, so you do it).

5. Confirm the claim: in Pinterest, Settings > Claimed accounts > Websites should show www.eaglebed.co.uk as Claimed. If the app claim fails, use Claim > Add HTML tag, and paste the <meta name="p:domain_verify" ...> tag inside <head> of theme.liquid (live theme, owner only), then press Verify.

6. Rich Pins: nothing to apply for. Once the domain is claimed, Pinterest reads the og:price tags already on every product page. After the first pins go live, open one on Pinterest and check that it shows the price and the www.eaglebed.co.uk link.
7. Create the 8 boards with the exact names in pin.json before uploading the CSV (names must match exactly, including 'é' and ':').
8. Optional: claim Instagram @eaglebed.co.uk, TikTok @eagle.bed and YouTube in Settings > Claimed accounts so their content is credited to Eagle Bed.

9. Upload pins: Pinterest > Create > Create Pin > Bulk create Pins (or Settings > Bulk create Pins) > upload pins.csv. Pinterest only schedules up to about 30 days ahead, so upload on or after 14 Nov 2026 and before 16 Nov 2026. Times are written in UK time (GMT, the same as UTC until late March).

catalogFeed.why: The Shopify Pinterest app builds the feed for you from all 145 live products, keeps prices and stock in step automatically, and turns each product into a free product pin with the price shown. It also makes the products eligible for Pinterest shopping surfaces. It costs nothing unless you choose to run Pinterest ads later (no ad spend is proposed here).
checks: After the first sync, open Pinterest Ads Manager > Catalogs > Data sources and fix any items flagged with errors (missing image, price, or description).
These are handmade beds with no barcodes; if Pinterest warns about missing GTIN, that is expected and not blocking.
Keep the 20 hand-made pins as well: catalog pins use the plain featured image, while the hand-made pins carry board keywords and better titles.
